newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PORTLAND WINS 11TH STRAIGHT OVER PLUMMETING BUCKS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PORTLAND WINS 11TH STRAIGHT OVER PLUMMETING BUCKS.

text.p: Two teams heading in opposite directions met in Milwaukee Thursday, and the soaring Portland Trail Blazers raced to a 97-78 victory over the plummeting Bucks.

Clifford Robinson scored 20 points and keyed big spurts in both halves, Rasheed Wallace also scored 20 points and Isaiah Rider added 15 as the Trail Blazers won their 11th straight. The Bucks have lost 12 of their last 14 games.

Portland has not lost since reports surfaced that coach P.J. Carlesimo would be fired. The Blazers matched their second-best defensive effort of the season, and the coach praised every facet of his team's game.
"Our defensive effort the entire night was good," Carlesimo said. "We were very unselfish. We looked for the extra pass and executed very well. We got after it on the boards."
Vin Baker scored 26 points and Glenn Robinson added 16 for the Bucks, who scored just 15 points in the third quarter and 34 in the second half.
"They are a strong, physical team, especially tonight," embattled Bucks coach Chris Ford said. "Their guards were able to penetrate and create at will. They have a very talented offence all around."
In Phoenix, Danny Manning made 10-of-15 shots from the field en route to 26 points and Kevin Johnson added 24 and 15 assists as the surging Suns defeated the reeling San Antonio Spurs, 113-106.

Cedric Ceballos added 23 points, including 10 in the third quarter, for the Suns, who have won four of five and nine of their last 13 games. They also have topped 100 points in eight straight contests.
The Suns improved to 20-14 at home and despite an 0-13 start, moved into a tie with the Sacramento Kings for the final playoff berth in the Western Conference.

In Houston, Hakeem Olajuwon scored 26 points and had a key block and jumper in the final two minutes, when the Rockets held the Washington Bullets scoreless for a 96-90 victory, their eighth in 10 games.
Clyde Drexler had 19 points and eight assists and four points down the stretch for Houston, which blew a 13-point halftime lead but limited Washington to just four points in the final 5 1/2 minutes.

Rod Strickland had 21 points and 10 assists for the Bullets, who had won four of their last five games but remained 3 1/2 games behind the Cavaliers, who hold the final playoff berth in the Eastern Conference.
At Cleveland, Eddie Jones scored 25 points and Nick Van Exel had 22 as the Los Angeles Lakers posted an 89-76 victory over the short-handed Cavaliers.
Elden Campbell added 18 points for Los Angeles, which has won three in a row and five of its last six games.

Bobby Phills tallied a season-high 27 points and Bob Sura had 19 and nine assists for Cleveland, which has dropped four of its last five contests. All-Star point guard Terrell Brandon missed his third straight game with a bruised tailbone amd forward Chris Mills sat out due to a sinus infection.

In Seattle, Hersey Hawkins had 10 of his 23 points in the first quarter and Denver committed an NBA season-high 33 turnovers as the SuperSonics roared away from the Nuggets 123-97, snapping a two-game losing streak.
Shawn Kemp had 24 points and 10 rebounds for the Sonics, who led by as many as 35 points in matching their season high for points in a game.
LaPhonso Ellis had 20 points and nine rebounds for Denver.
In Orlando, Dennis Scott hit a tie-breaking three-pointer and Rony Seikaly hit a pair of free throws as the Magic handed the Golden State Warriors another close loss, 100-95.
Seikaly finished with 28 points for the Magic, who have defeated Golden State five straight times at home. Scott added 21 points and Anfernee Hardaway 20.

Joe Smith scored 24 points to lead the Warriors, who failed to hold a lead in the final minute for the second straight game. Golden State blew an eight-point lead with less than 90 seconds to go in regulation Wednesday at Miami and has lost 12 of its last 17 games.
